# Page: https://myunimentor.in/

Career guidance for Class 11–12 students 

## Right guidance. Right fit. Right university. 

Choosing a stream, course and university is one of the biggest decisions a student makes — yet most still make it on hearsay. MyUniMentor brings honest, expert career guidance to students across India, one-on-one and in schools, so every student decides with clarity.

Partner with us

## Meet our founder 
“When I was in school, nobody explained where a course actually leads. I had to research everything on my own. Good schools have always been everywhere — organised career guidance hasn't.” 

Om Garg , Founder, MyUniMentor 
View Om's profile Invite Om for a session 

## Frequently asked questions 
Still unsure? Call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070 . 
What is MyUniMentor? 
MyUniMentor is a career counselling and admissions guidance organisation that works with students across India, online and in person, from its base in Dehradun, Uttarakhand. It helps Class 11–12 students choose the right stream, course and university, runs free career seminars for schools, and organises the School Career Guidance Summit, where universities meet students inside their schools. 
Can I get career counselling online from anywhere in India? 
Yes. MyUniMentor counsels students anywhere in India online, and in person in Dehradun and Saharanpur. The first one-on-one session is free. Book through this website, or call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070. 
How do I choose a good career counsellor? 
Choose one who asks about your marks, interests and plans before suggesting anything, explains every option with its entrance exams, does not push a single university, and is clear about any fees upfront. MyUniMentor’s first session is free, so you can judge for yourself. 
Is career counselling at MyUniMentor free for students? 
Yes. The first one-on-one counselling session is free for Class 11–12 students. Book through the form on this website, or call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070. 
Are MyUniMentor's career seminars free for schools? 
Yes. Career guidance seminars for Class 11–12 students are offered free of cost to schools. 
Which cities does MyUniMentor work in? 
MyUniMentor works with schools in Dehradun (Uttarakhand) and Saharanpur (Uttar Pradesh), and counsels students across India online and offline. In 2027, we plan to expand to Rishikesh, Roorkee, Srinagar and the wider Garhwal region. 
What is the School Career Guidance Summit? 
It is an in-school career fair organised by MyUniMentor. Universities set up stalls on the school campus and Class 11–12 students meet them, ask questions and compare options without leaving the school campus. The first edition ran across 12 schools in Dehradun and Saharanpur in October 2026. 
How can a university partner with MyUniMentor? 
Universities can exhibit at the School Career Guidance Summit and use MyUniMentor's admission and outreach support. 32 universities are currently partners. Send an enquiry through the partnership form or email info@myunimentor.in. 

## Not sure which course or university is right for you? 
Talk to a counsellor. 1-on-1 counselling is free for students. 
Book a free session Call +91 74175 57070

# Page: https://myunimentor.in/about

Home / About 

## Career guidance for every student 

Our mission is simple: every student in India should get honest, expert guidance before choosing a stream, a course or a university, wherever they live and whichever school they go to. 

## Why we exist 

For most students in India, the biggest decision of their life is made on hearsay: a relative's advice, a coaching brochure, what a friend is picking. 

Real career guidance has always been a privilege. Some students get a counsellor, a career fair and someone to explain where a course actually leads. Most never do. 

MyUniMentor exists to change that. We want guidance to reach every single student, through one-on-one counselling, free tools anyone can use, and sessions in schools and communities. 

## How guidance reaches every student 
Four ways in, so no student is left without help. 

- 

## One-on-one counselling 
Online or in person, for students anywhere in India. Your first session is free. Book a session 
- 

## Free tools and guides 
The 2027 entrance exam calendar, course guides and articles, open to everyone. See the exam calendar 
- 

## Seminars and summits 
Free career seminars and the School Career Guidance Summit, held on the school's own campus. For schools 
- 

## A national university network 
32 partner universities across India, so students compare real options before they decide. See the network 

## What we believe 

- 1 

## Every student, not a few 
Good guidance shouldn't depend on your city, your school or who your family knows. 
- 2 

## Fit over hype 
The right course is the one that fits you, not the one everyone around you is picking. 
- 3 

## Clarity before deadlines 
Decisions made early and calmly are better than decisions made the night before a form closes.

## About Om Garg 

When Om was in school, there was no one to explain where a course actually leads. He had to research everything on his own. 

That experience shaped his work. Om spent five years in a senior cross-functional role in the education sector, guiding students and speaking at schools, before founding MyUniMentor in Dehradun in 2026. 

Today he leads MyUniMentor's mission of bringing honest, expert career guidance to every student in India, through one-on-one counselling, free tools and guides, and sessions in schools.

## About Om Garg 
Still unsure? Call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070 . 
Who is Om Garg? 
Om Garg is the founder of MyUniMentor, a career counselling and admissions guidance organisation based in Dehradun, Uttarakhand. A BBA graduate and Olympus High alumnus, he has guided over 10,000 students, delivered 100+ career seminars and counselled 500+ students one-on-one. 
What does Om Garg do? 
Om leads MyUniMentor and works directly with Class 11–12 students and parents on choosing a stream, a course and a university. He also speaks at schools and runs the School Career Guidance Summit. 
Where is Om Garg based? 
Om is based in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, and works with students across India, online and in person. 
How can I invite Om Garg to my school? 
Send an invitation through the MyUniMentor contact page or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070. Career seminars are free for schools.

## Career counselling for students and parents 

One-on-one guidance to choose the right stream, course and university — so you decide with clarity, not on hearsay. 1-on-1 counselling is free for students. 

## Clarity before you choose 
Our counsellors sit with the student (and parents, if they like) to understand marks, interests, strengths and budget, then build a clear plan for what to study and where. 

- Free 1-on-1 counselling for students 
- Stream and subject choice for Class 11 
- Course and career path planning 
- A university shortlist that fits your marks, interests and budget 
- Guidance on entrance exams, applications and admissions 
- Online or in person 

## How it works 
- 1 

## Book a session 
Fill the form or WhatsApp us. We'll call you to fix a time. 
- 2 

## Understand the student 
Interests, strengths, marks and goals — in a one-on-one conversation. 
- 3 

## Build the plan 
Stream, course and career options, with a shortlist of universities that fit. 
- 4 

## Apply with support 
Help with entrance exams, applications and admission steps. 

## Get started 
Tell us a little about yourself and our team will call you back. 

- Call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070 
- Email info@myunimentor.in

## Frequently asked questions 
Still unsure? Call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070 . 
Is career counselling free? 
Yes. Your first one-on-one counselling session is free for Class 11–12 students. 
Who is the free session for? 
Students currently in Class 11 or Class 12, along with their parents or guardians. 
Is counselling online or in person? 
Both. We counsel students in person and online, anywhere in India. 
Can parents join the session? 
Yes, parents are welcome and encouraged to join.

## Career guidance for schools 

Free career seminars and the School Career Guidance Summit — organised career guidance for your Class 11–12 students, on your own campus. 

## Bring career guidance to your campus 
We run career guidance seminars for Class 11–12 students at no cost to the school, and bring universities to your campus through the School Career Guidance Summit. 

- Career guidance seminars for Class 11–12, free for schools 
- The School Career Guidance Summit on your campus 
- Universities set up stalls; students meet them without leaving the school campus 
- Planned around your timetable, within 2.5 hours 
- Your school provides the stage and AV; we handle the rest 

## How it works 
- 1 

## Get in touch 
Send an enquiry or call us to pick a date. 
- 2 

## We plan it with you 
Session format, timing and student groups, around your timetable. 
- 3 

## On the day 
Our team runs the seminar or the summit on your campus. 
- 4 

## Follow-up 
Students who want one-on-one guidance can book a counselling session.

## Admission and outreach support for universities 

Meet serious Class 11–12 students where they already are — inside their schools — through one partner. 

## Reach students through their schools 
MyUniMentor works with 12 schools across Dehradun and Saharanpur. Partner universities meet their Class 11–12 students at the School Career Guidance Summit and through our admission-season outreach. 

- A stall at the School Career Guidance Summit in our partner schools 
- Focused, school-sized fairs, so your stall gets real attention 
- Reach students across Dehradun and Saharanpur through one partner 
- Admission-season outreach support 
- Expanding to Rishikesh, Roorkee, Srinagar and Garhwal in 2027 

## How it works 
- 1 

## Enquire 
Tell us which cities and schools you want to reach. 
- 2 

## Choose your participation 
Pick the schools and dates that suit your admission plans. 
- 3 

## Meet students 
Your team meets Class 11–12 students at your stall on campus. 
- 4 

## Stay in touch 
Admission-season outreach support through the cycle. 

## The people behind the stalls

Which universities exhibit at each school? 
The line-up is chosen for each school and varies by city. 
Do universities get stage time at the Career Summit? 
No. Universities take part through exhibitor stalls only, so students can meet each one directly. 
Which universities are already partners?

# Page: https://myunimentor.in/career-summit

Home / Career Summit 

## School Career Guidance Summit 

The first edition ran in October 2026 across 12 schools. An in-school career fair. Universities set up stalls on the school campus and Class 11–12 students meet them, ask questions and compare options — without leaving the school campus. 
12 Schools 2,000+ Students reached 2027 Planned: Garhwal region 

## The people behind the stalls 
Admissions teams from our partner universities with the MyUniMentor team, at the wrap-up of the 2026 edition at Saigrace Academy International, Dehradun. 

32 partner universities Every stall at the Summit was run by a university's own admissions team. See all partner universities 

## A career fair, inside the school 
Most career fairs ask students to travel to a city hall. The Career Summit comes to them — so every Class 11–12 student in the school gets to meet universities in person. 

- Partner universities set up stalls on the school campus 
- Each university's own delegates give first-hand information on courses, fees and admissions 
- Students get their doubts cleared on the spot, one-to-one 
- Parents and teachers can join in and ask questions too 
- Completed within 2.5 hours, including setup 
- The first edition ran in October 2026 across Dehradun and Saharanpur

## Exam questions students ask 
Still unsure? Call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070 . 
When is JEE Main 2027? 
JEE Main 2027 Session 1 is scheduled for 20–24 and 28 January 2027. The last date to apply is 22 November 2026 (with late fee until 26 November). Session 2 is scheduled for 2–7 April 2027. Read our JEE Main Session 1 guide . 
When is JEE Advanced 2027? 
JEE Advanced 2027 will be held on 23 May 2027, organised by IIT Delhi. Only the top JEE Main candidates are eligible to appear. 
When is NEET UG 2027? 
NTA has not announced the NEET UG 2027 date yet. NEET is usually held on the first Sunday of May. 
When is CUET UG 2027? 
CUET UG 2027 has not been announced yet. It is expected in May 2027, and registration is usually open in January–February. Read our CUET guide . 
When is CLAT 2027? 
CLAT 2027 is on 6 December 2026. Applications closed on 31 October 2026. See our law after 12th guide . 
When are the design entrance exams (NID DAT, NIFT, UCEED) for 2027? 
NID DAT 2027 Prelims is on 20 December 2026 (last date to apply: 30 November 2026). NIFT 2027 is on 10 January 2027 (tentative; applications extended to 24 November 2026) and UCEED 2027 is on 17 January 2027. See our B.Des guide . 
When is the CHRIST University entrance test for 2027? 
The CHRIST University online entrance test for UG 2027 admissions is on 5 December 2026. The last date to apply for entrance-test programmes is 25 November 2026 (5 pm), and skill assessment and interviews run from 11 to 13 December 2026. 
When is IPMAT 2027? 
IPMAT Indore 2027 is on 24 April 2027. Registration dates are awaited. It is the entrance exam for the five-year integrated management programme at IIM Indore. 
When are NMIMS NPAT and Symbiosis SET 2027? 
Neither has been announced yet. For reference, NPAT 2026 was held from 10 February to 31 May 2026, and Symbiosis SET 2026 on 2 and 10 May 2026 (registration closed on 15 April). We will add the 2027 dates as soon as NMIMS and Symbiosis publish them. 
When are JIPMAT and the IISER Aptitude Test 2027? 
Neither has been announced yet. JIPMAT 2026 (for the integrated management programmes at IIM Bodh Gaya and IIM Jammu) and the IISER Aptitude Test 2026 were both held on 7 June 2026, so both are expected around June 2027. 
When do the CBSE and CISCE board exams 2027 start? 
CBSE Class 10 and 12 exams start on 16 February 2027; Class 12 ends on 9 April. ISC (Class 12) runs from 9 February to 8 April 2027, and ICSE (Class 10) from 15 February to 31 March 2027. See the full CBSE Class 12 , CBSE Class 10 , ISC and ICSE date sheets. 
Which entrance exams can Commerce and Humanities students take? 
CUET UG (for central and many other universities), CLAT and AILET (law), IPMAT and JIPMAT (integrated management), and NID DAT, NIFT and UCEED (design) are all open to Commerce and Humanities students. JEE and NEET need Science subjects. 
Can PCB students take JEE, or PCM students take NEET? 
B.Tech admissions through JEE generally need Physics, Chemistry and Maths in Class 12, so PCB students usually focus on NEET, CUET and other exams. NEET needs Biology, so PCM students are not eligible. PCMB students can take both. 
How often is this exam calendar updated? 
We check every date against the official websites regularly. This calendar was last checked on 25 November 2026. Always confirm on the official website before you apply. 
Which exam should I take? 
It depends on your stream and the course you want. Book free 1-on-1 counselling and a counsellor will map out your exam plan with you. 

## Not sure which exams you should take? 
A counsellor will build your exam plan with you. 1-on-1 counselling is free for students. 
Book a free session Call +91 74175 57070

## Free career check 

For Class 9–12. About four minutes. The questions change with your stream and your answers, then show the career paths, courses and entrance exams that fit you. 

## Guides that go with your result 
Free guides on courses, streams and entrance exams, written for Class 9–12 students and parents. 

- Entrance exam calendar 
- Partner universities 
- CUET UG guide 
- Choosing a stream after Class 10 
- B.Tech CSE after 12th 
- BCA after 12th 
- Engineering branches explained 
- B.Des after 12th 
- Careers after PCB beyond MBBS 
- B.Com (Hons) after 12th 
- BBA after 12th 
- Law after 12th 
- MyUniMentor logo 
- Contact 
- Your account 
- Psychometric test 

## About the career check 
Still unsure? Call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070 . 
Is the MyUniMentor career check free? 
Yes. It is free and takes about four minutes. You share your name and phone number before you see your result, and a MyUniMentor counsellor calls you to talk it through. 
Who is it for? 
Students in Class 9, 10, 11 and 12. Class 9 and 10 students also see which stream fits each career path. 
How is it different from other career tests? 
The questions change with your stream and your answers. Commerce, PCM, PCB, PCMB and Humanities students each get their own set of activities, and the check then asks follow-up questions only about your top areas. 
Can I save my result? 
Yes. If you are logged in to your free MyUniMentor account, your result is saved to it automatically. If not, tap Save to my account on the result, log in with your email, and it is saved there. You can open the full result again anytime from your dashboard. 
Is this a psychometric test? 
No. It is a short guidance tool based on your interests, stream and plans. For a detailed picture, take the MyUniMentor career psychometric test : about 25 minutes, with personality, aptitude and values, and a full report.

# Page: https://myunimentor.in/psychometric-test

Home / Psychometric test 

## Career psychometric test 

For Class 9–12. About 25 minutes. Interests, aptitude, personality and values, matched to Indian courses and entrance exams, with a detailed report. ₹99, or free when three friends join. 
Start the test See a sample report 

- 25 min Save and resume anytime 
- 6 parts 95 questions and a speed round 
- 24 areas Matched to Indian courses and exams 
- ₹99 Or free with 3 friends 

## What the test measures 
Six short parts. Interests tell you what you will enjoy, aptitude what comes easily to you, personality how you like to work, and values what you want from a job. 

- 1 

## Interests 
36 activities 
How much would you enjoy fixing a scooter, writing a script, running a stall or caring for patients? Scored on Holland’s six interest types (RIASEC), the model behind most career tests worldwide. 
- 2 

## Personality 
25 statements 
Social energy, warmth, discipline, calm under pressure and curiosity: the Big Five, measured with free research scales from the International Personality Item Pool. 
- 3 

## Aptitude 
6 timed sections 
Numbers, words, patterns, shapes you turn in your mind, gears and levers, and a one-minute speed check. About 12 minutes in all. 
- 4 

## Situations 
6 real moments 
Falling behind before boards, a teammate who isn’t pulling their weight, a hard problem you can’t crack. What you would really do. 
- 5 

## Values 
Rank 6 
Achievement, independence, recognition, relationships, support and working conditions: the six work values used by O*NET. 
- 6 

## About you 
1 minute 
Your class, stream, marks band, favourite subjects and how long you want to study, so every suggestion is one you can actually take. 

## Sample questions 
A taste of each part. The real test has 95 questions and a one-minute speed round. 
Interests 
How much would you enjoy this? Build a working model, like a robot, a drone or a bridge Strongly dislike Dislike Not sure Like Strongly like 
Personality 
How much is this like you? I pay attention to details. Not like me at all Not much In between Quite like me Very much 
Aptitude: logical reasoning 
Which figure comes next? ? 
Aptitude: mechanical reasoning 
Gear A has 20 teeth and turns gear B, which has 40 teeth. When A turns 10 times, how many times does B turn? 5 10 20 40 
Situations 
A classmate who is usually cheerful has been quiet and alone for a few days. What do you do? 
- Sit with them and gently ask if everything is okay 
- Tell a teacher you are worried about them 
- Give them space; they will talk if they want to 
- Assume it is not your business 

## How we match you to careers 

Every career area has a profile. For interests, we use the U.S. Department of Labor’s O*NET interest codes for related jobs: software developers and data scientists are “Investigative and Conventional”, lawyers “Enterprising, Conventional and Investigative”, physiotherapists “Social, Investigative and Realistic”. 

Your answers are compared with each profile and weighted like this: 

- 50% Interests 
- 25% Aptitude 
- 15% Personality 
- 10% Values 

Subjects you enjoy add a little. If you are in Class 11 or 12 and a path needs a different stream, it is marked clearly, so you only plan around options open to you. 

Sample report 
Riya, here is your report 
Interest code IAS Top match Psychology 

Investigative 
Artistic 
Social 
Enterprising 
Realistic 
Conventional 

Strong fit · 82% 

## What is in your report 
Ten sections on screen and as a PDF you can download, print and share. 
- Your top five career paths with a fit score, why each one suits you, what to keep in mind, and the courses, course lengths and entrance exams for each 
- Your interest code your three strongest interest types, like IAS or ECS, and what they mean for the work you will enjoy 
- Your aptitudes six bands from Building to Strong, with what to practise 
- Your personality five traits, each with a strength and a tip 
- How you handle situations your strengths and what is worth working on 
- Your values what you want from work, and the fields that offer it 
- Paths to think twice about the areas that came lowest for you 
- How to study, for you methods with strong research behind them, picked for your profile 
- Your next 90 days a plan for your class: Class 9–10, Class 11, or Class 12 and gap year 
- How the report works the methods and sources behind every score 

See what a report looks like 

## What we leave out, and why 

No fingerprint (DMIT) tests. There is no scientific evidence that fingerprints predict talent or careers. 

No “learning styles”. Reviews of the research have found no good evidence that teaching to a visual or auditory “style” helps. We give study tips with strong evidence instead, like testing yourself and spacing out revision. 

No personality “types”. We measure traits on a scale, because people are rarely one type or the other. 

## Its limits, honestly 
Each section is short, so treat scores as bands, not exact numbers. Aptitudes grow with practice. And for now we compare you with your own profile; comparisons with other students will be added once enough students have taken the test. That is why every report ends with a free session with a counsellor. 

## How to take it 

- 1 

## Create your free account 
Log in with your email. No password needed. 

- 2 

## Unlock the test 
Pay ₹99, use an access code, or share your invite link: when three friends sign up with it, your test is free. 

- 3 

## Take it and get your report 
About 25 minutes. Your report is ready the moment you finish, and saved in your account. 

Just want a quick idea first? Try the free 4-minute career check . 

## About the psychometric test 
Still unsure? Call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070 . 
What is a psychometric test for career guidance? 
A set of questions that measures your interests, abilities, personality and values, and then matches them to careers. MyUniMentor’s test takes about 25 minutes and matches you to 24 career areas, with the courses and entrance exams for each. 
Who is it for? 
Students in Class 9, 10, 11 and 12, and students taking a gap year. Class 9 and 10 students also see which stream each career path needs. 
How much does it cost? 
₹99, paid once. You can also unlock it free: share your invite link, and when three friends create free MyUniMentor accounts with it, your test unlocks. Schools and events may also give you an access code. 
Can I stop and finish later? 
Yes. Your answers save as you go to your free MyUniMentor account, so you can stop anytime and continue on any device. Each timed aptitude section keeps its remaining time. 
How accurate is it? 
It is a guidance tool, not a final answer. Interests are the strongest single guide to a career you will enjoy, which is why they carry half the weight. Each section is short, so read scores as rough bands, and talk your report through with a counsellor before deciding. 
Can my parents see the report? 
Yes, if you link your accounts. A parent who links to your account from their own MyUniMentor account can open your report once you finish. 
Do you use DMIT or fingerprint tests? 
No. Fingerprint-based tests (DMIT) are not backed by scientific evidence, and neither are “learning styles”. We leave both out. 
How is it different from the free career check? 
The free career check takes about 4 minutes and looks at your interests and plans. The psychometric test takes about 25 minutes and adds personality, six timed aptitude sections, real-life situations and values, with a much more detailed report. 

## Ready to find your best-fit career? 
About 25 minutes. Your report is ready the moment you finish. 
Start the test Call +91 74175 57070

## BBA after 12th 

BBA is a management degree that teaches how businesses and organisations run, from marketing and finance to people and operations. It is one of the most popular choices after Class 12, open to students from every stream. 

- Duration 
3 years, or 4 with honours at many universities 
- Stream 
Any stream 
- Entrance 
CUET UG, IPMAT, JIPMAT or university tests 
- Next step 
MBA or a management role 

## What you study in BBA 
- Principles of management and organisational behaviour 
- Marketing, sales and consumer behaviour 
- Financial accounting and corporate finance 
- Human resource management 
- Business economics, statistics and business law 
- Entrepreneurship, projects and internships 

## Who BBA suits 
BBA is a good fit if you: 
- Enjoy leading groups and presenting ideas 
- Want to start or grow a business one day 
- Plan to do an MBA 
- Prefer case studies and projects over heavy theory 

## Specialisations 
Common specialisations include Marketing, Finance, Human Resources, International Business, Business Analytics and Digital Marketing. The specialisation shapes your career path, so compare what each university offers. 

## Entrance exams and eligibility 
Many universities admit BBA students through CUET UG . Some private universities run their own tests or admit on Class 12 marks. For the five-year Integrated Programme in Management at IIMs, you'll need IPMAT or JIPMAT , which test maths and verbal ability. 
MyUniMentor tip 
Eligibility, fees and admission routes differ from one university to the next. Check each university's admission page, and use our 12 questions to ask a university before you pay anything. 

## Careers after BBA 
- Marketing and brand management 
- Sales and business development 
- Human resources 
- Operations and supply chain 
- Financial analysis 
- Entrepreneurship or a family business

## BBA: common questions 
Still unsure? Call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070 . 
Can a Science or Humanities student do BBA? 
Yes. BBA is open to students from all streams at most universities. 
Is Maths compulsory for BBA? 
Not at most universities. Some analytics or finance specialisations, and IPMAT for IIM programmes, expect Maths. Check the course you are targeting. 
Is BBA without an MBA enough? 
Many BBA graduates start working straight away in sales, marketing, HR or operations. An MBA later can help you move into senior management.

## B.Tech CSE after 12th 

B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) is a four-year engineering degree focused on programming, software and computing systems. It is the most sought-after engineering branch in India. 

- Duration 
4 years 
- Stream 
PCM (Physics, Chemistry, Maths) 
- Entrance 
JEE Main, JEE Advanced or university tests 
- Next step 
Tech jobs, M.Tech or MS 

## What you study in B.Tech CSE 
- Programming in languages like C, Python and Java 
- Data structures and algorithms 
- Databases and operating systems 
- Computer networks and cyber security 
- Software engineering 
- Electives in AI, machine learning, cloud and data science 

## Who B.Tech CSE suits 
B.Tech CSE is a good fit if you: 
- Enjoy logical problem-solving and puzzles 
- Like building things with code 
- Are comfortable with Maths 
- Can spend long hours practising and debugging 

## Specialisations 
Many universities offer CSE with specialisations such as Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, Data Science, Cyber Security or Cloud Computing. If you are unsure, core CSE keeps the most options open. Read engineering branches explained to compare. 

## Entrance exams and eligibility 
IITs admit through JEE Advanced . NITs, IIITs and many other institutes admit through JEE Main . Many private universities accept JEE Main scores, run their own entrance tests or consider Class 12 marks. See the 2027 exam calendar . 
MyUniMentor tip 
Eligibility, fees and admission routes differ from one university to the next. Check each university's admission page, and use our 12 questions to ask a university before you pay anything. 

## Careers after B.Tech CSE 
- Software developer or engineer 
- Data scientist or analyst 
- AI and machine learning engineer 
- Cyber security specialist 
- Cloud and DevOps engineer 
- Product roles or your own startup

## B.Tech CSE: common questions 
Still unsure? Call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070 . 
Can I do B.Tech CSE without Maths? 
No. B.Tech requires Physics, Chemistry and Maths in Class 12. 
Is CSE with AI better than core CSE? 
Not necessarily. It adds focused courses, but core CSE covers the same foundations and keeps more options open. 
Do I need JEE for private universities? 
Not always. Many private universities accept JEE Main, but many also run their own tests or admit on Class 12 marks.

Home / Course guides 

## Law (BA LLB) after 12th 

You can start studying law right after Class 12 through a five-year integrated degree, such as BA LLB or BBA LLB. It combines a bachelor's degree with a law degree and prepares you to practise as a lawyer. 

- Duration 
5 years (integrated) 
- Stream 
Any stream 
- Entrance 
CLAT, AILET or university tests 
- Next step 
Practice, corporate law or LLM 

## What you study in Law (BA LLB) 
- Constitutional law and the Indian legal system 
- Contracts, torts and criminal law 
- Corporate and commercial law 
- Property, family and labour law 
- Moot courts, legal research and writing 
- Internships with lawyers, firms and courts 

## Who Law (BA LLB) suits 
Law (BA LLB) is a good fit if you: 
- Enjoy reading and arguing a point 
- Are curious about rules, rights and justice 
- Write and speak clearly 
- Can read long texts with focus 

## Specialisations 
Choose BA LLB if you are drawn to subjects like political science and history. Choose BBA LLB if you are interested in business and corporate law. Both lead to the same LLB qualification. 

## Entrance exams and eligibility 
CLAT is the main exam for National Law Universities. CLAT 2027 has 120 multiple-choice questions in 2 hours across five sections: English, current affairs, legal reasoning, logical reasoning and quantitative techniques. Wrong answers cost 0.25 marks. NLU Delhi uses AILET , and many universities run their own tests. See the exam calendar . 
MyUniMentor tip 
Eligibility, fees and admission routes differ from one university to the next. Check each university's admission page, and use our 12 questions to ask a university before you pay anything. 

## Careers after Law (BA LLB) 
- Litigation in courts 
- Corporate lawyer in a law firm or company 
- Judicial services (judge) 
- Legal advisor or in-house counsel 
- Policy, research and public interest law 
- Legal journalism or academics 

Want to see if Law (BA LLB) fits you? Talk to a counsellor or explore our 32 partner universities .

## Law (BA LLB): common questions 
Still unsure? Call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070 . 
Can a Science or Commerce student study law? 
Yes. Integrated law programmes are open to students from all streams. 
Do I need to know law before CLAT? 
No. CLAT's legal reasoning section gives you the rules in the passage. It tests reasoning and reading, not prior legal knowledge. 
What is the difference between BA LLB and LLB? 
BA LLB is a five-year integrated degree you start after Class 12. LLB is a three-year degree you can take after completing any graduation.

## B.Des after 12th 

A Bachelor of Design (B.Des) trains you to solve problems creatively, whether that means a product, a space, a garment, a brand or an app. It is open to students from every stream and rewards creativity more than marks. 

- Duration 
4 years 
- Stream 
Any stream 
- Entrance 
NID DAT, UCEED, NIFT or university tests 
- Next step 
Design studio, in-house role or M.Des 

## What you study in B.Des 
- Drawing, sketching and visual thinking 
- Design principles, colour and materials 
- Design research and user understanding 
- Digital tools for design and prototyping 
- Studio projects in your specialisation 
- Portfolio building and internships 

## Who B.Des suits 
B.Des is a good fit if you: 
- Love drawing, making or rearranging things 
- Notice how things look and work 
- Enjoy open-ended problems with no single answer 
- Are ready to build a portfolio 

## Specialisations 
Popular specialisations include Fashion Design, Interior Design, Product Design, Communication Design, UX and Interaction Design, and Animation. Each leads to a distinct career, so choose based on the kind of work you enjoy making. 

## Entrance exams and eligibility 
NID DAT is for the National Institutes of Design. UCEED is for design programmes at IITs and other institutes. NIFT runs its own entrance for fashion and design. Many private universities run their own design aptitude tests and portfolio reviews. See the exam calendar . 
MyUniMentor tip 
Eligibility, fees and admission routes differ from one university to the next. Check each university's admission page, and use our 12 questions to ask a university before you pay anything. 

## Careers after B.Des 
- Fashion designer 
- Interior designer 
- Product or industrial designer 
- UX/UI designer 
- Graphic and brand designer 
- Animator or visual artist

## B.Des: common questions 
Still unsure? Call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070 . 
Can a Commerce or Science student do B.Des? 
Yes. B.Des is open to all streams. Entrance exams test creativity and design aptitude, not school subjects. 
Do I need to be good at drawing? 
Basic drawing helps, and it improves with practice. Design exams also test observation, ideas and problem-solving. 
Is B.Des the same as B.Arch? 
No. B.Arch is a five-year architecture degree, usually requiring Maths and the NATA or JEE Paper 2 exam. B.Des covers many design fields and is open to all streams.

## B.Com (Hons) after 12th 

B.Com (Hons) is a commerce degree that goes deep into accounting, finance, taxation and economics. It is a strong foundation for careers in finance and for professional courses like CA. 

- Duration 
3 years, or 4 with honours at many universities 
- Stream 
Commerce preferred; some accept others 
- Entrance 
CUET UG, university tests or Class 12 marks 
- Next step 
CA, CS, CMA, M.Com or MBA 

## What you study in B.Com (Hons) 
- Financial and corporate accounting 
- Income tax and GST 
- Corporate finance and financial markets 
- Auditing 
- Business law and company law 
- Economics and business statistics 

## Who B.Com (Hons) suits 
B.Com (Hons) is a good fit if you: 
- Enjoy Accountancy and numbers 
- Plan to pursue CA, CS or CMA 
- Want a career in banking, finance or audit 
- Like understanding how money moves in a business 

## Specialisations 
Some universities offer B.Com with specialisations like FinTech, Banking and Insurance, International Finance or Accounting and Taxation. Compare these before you apply. 

## Entrance exams and eligibility 
Central universities and many others admit B.Com students through CUET UG . Some private universities run their own tests or admit on Class 12 marks. Many students register for CA Foundation alongside their degree.

What is the difference between B.Com and B.Com (Hons)? 
B.Com (Hons) usually goes deeper into fewer core subjects, with more focus on accounting and finance. Many universities now offer four-year honours degrees under NEP. 
Can I do CA with B.Com?

## BCA after 12th 

BCA (Bachelor of Computer Applications) is a computer science degree focused on programming and software applications. It is a popular route into IT for students who want a tech career without a four-year engineering degree. 

- Duration 
3 years, or 4 with honours at many universities 
- Stream 
Often requires Maths; some accept any stream 
- Entrance 
CUET UG, university tests or Class 12 marks 
- Next step 
IT jobs, MCA or MBA 

## What you study in BCA 
- Programming in C, Java and Python 
- Data structures and databases 
- Web development 
- Operating systems and networking 
- Software engineering 
- Electives in data science, cloud or cyber security 

## Who BCA suits 
BCA is a good fit if you: 
- Enjoy computers and want to code 
- Want a tech career in three years 
- Are from Science or Commerce with Maths 
- Like practical, project-based work 

## Specialisations 
Some universities offer BCA with specialisations in Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Cloud Computing or Cyber Security. A strong project portfolio matters as much as the specialisation. 

## Entrance exams and eligibility 
Many universities admit BCA students through CUET UG , their own entrance tests or Class 12 marks. Many require Maths in Class 12, so check eligibility before you apply.

Is BCA equal to B.Tech CSE?

Source: DITU fee details (2026-27). 

## Scholarships 
First-year merit scholarships on tuition: 100% for 95% and above in Class 12 (PCM/relevant subjects) or a JEE rank up to 50,000; 50% for 90–95% or JEE rank 50,001–80,000; 25% for 80–90% or JEE rank 80,001–1,00,000. There is also a 25% tuition scholarship for students from Uttarakhand and Himalayan states. 
Source: DITU scholarships.

Still unsure? Call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070 . 
How do I get admission to Haridwar University in 2027? 
B.Tech (Hons.): HUAET (Haridwar University's admission test) or other eligible routes; lateral entry for diploma holders in CSE, AI & ML and ECE. Eligibility: Class 12 with Physics, Maths and Chemistry/Computer Science, 45% (40% reserved). MyUniMentor gives free admission guidance: send an enquiry or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070. 
What are the fees at Haridwar University? 
For 2026-27, B.Tech (Hons.) CSE tuition is ₹62,000 a year, with a first-year total of ₹1,32,000; B.Tech AI & ML costs ₹1,62,000 in the first year. 
What scholarships does Haridwar University offer? 
25% of first-year tuition for Uttarakhand domicile students and for girls (2026 and 2027 Class 12 pass-outs), with merit scholarships on marks and JEE or CUET percentiles. Only one scholarship per student. 
Does Haridwar University have hostels? 
Separate hostels for boys and girls. Hostel fee, including mess and laundry, is ₹85,000 a year for a normal room, ₹95,000 semi-deluxe and ₹1,05,000 deluxe AC.

## How to choose the right stream after Class 10 

Choosing a stream after Class 10 is the first big academic decision most students make. It decides which subjects you study for two years and which courses stay open after Class 12. Here is how to make the choice with clarity instead of pressure. 

By Om Garg , Founder, MyUniMentor · Updated 20 Nov 2026 · 7 min read 

## The three streams, and what each one opens 

Most schools offer three streams. Each keeps some doors open and closes others, so it helps to know where each one leads before you pick. 

Stream Core subjects Courses it leads to 

Science (PCM) Physics, Chemistry, Maths Engineering (B.Tech), Architecture, BCA, B.Sc in Physics, Maths or Computer Science, Data Science, and most Commerce and Humanities courses too 

Science (PCB) Physics, Chemistry, Biology MBBS, BDS, Nursing, Pharmacy, Physiotherapy, Biotechnology, Allied Health, Agriculture, and most Humanities courses 

Commerce Accountancy, Business Studies, Economics (Maths optional) B.Com, BBA, CA, CS, CMA, Economics, Integrated MBA (IPM), Law 

Humanities History, Political Science, Psychology, Sociology, English and more BA, Law, Journalism and Mass Communication, Psychology, Design, Civil Services preparation 

Some schools also offer PCMB (all four science subjects). It keeps both engineering and medicine open, but it is a heavy workload. Pick it only if you genuinely enjoy both Maths and Biology. 

## Start with what you enjoy, not what others pick 

The most common mistake we see in schools is choosing a stream because friends are choosing it, or because one stream is seen as "better". There is no better stream. There is only the stream that fits you. 

Ask yourself three honest questions: 

- Which subjects do I enjoy studying even when there is no exam? Interest keeps you going through two demanding years. 

- Which subjects do I do well in? Look at your Class 9 and 10 marks subject by subject, not just the overall percentage. 

- What kind of work can I imagine doing? Building things, treating people, running a business, writing, designing, arguing a case. You don't need a fixed career yet, just a direction. 

## The Maths question 

Maths deserves a separate decision because it quietly keeps many doors open. Engineering, BCA, Data Science, Economics (Hons) at many universities, and the IPMAT for integrated management programmes all expect Maths in Class 12. 

If you are choosing Commerce and you are comfortable with Maths, take it. If Maths genuinely worries you, Commerce without Maths and Humanities still lead to strong careers. Just know which courses you are closing before you decide. 
MyUniMentor tip 
Before you finalise, list three courses you might want after Class 12. Check that your stream and subjects make you eligible for all three. If one isn't covered, rethink the subject combination now, not in Class 12. 

## How parents can help 

Parents often have the most experience but the oldest information. Many careers that are popular today, like UX design, data science or sports management, barely existed as degree courses twenty years ago. The best support is a conversation, not a decision made for the student: 

- Ask your child what they enjoy, and listen before suggesting. 

- Share your concerns about stability or cost openly, so they can be weighed. 

- Talk to someone who knows today's courses and admission routes before you decide. 

## Can you change your stream later? 

Yes, to an extent. Science students can move into almost any Commerce or Humanities course after Class 12. Moving the other way, from Commerce or Humanities into Science courses like engineering or medicine, is very difficult because those courses require Science subjects in Class 12. That is why the choice matters most for students who are unsure about Science. 

## A simple way to decide 

- Note your favourite subjects and your strongest subjects. 

- Write down two or three career areas that interest you. 

- Check which stream keeps all of them open. 

- Decide on Maths separately. 

- Discuss it with your parents and a counsellor, then commit. 

Not sure where your interests point? Book a free counselling session and a counsellor will help you map your interests to a stream.

## Questions students ask 
Still unsure? Call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070 . 
Which stream is best after Class 10? 
No stream is best for everyone. Science (PCM or PCB), Commerce and Humanities each lead to strong careers. The right stream is the one that matches your interests, your strengths and the courses you may want after Class 12. 
Can a Commerce student do BCA or B.Tech? 
B.Tech requires Physics, Chemistry and Maths in Class 12, so Commerce students are not eligible. Many universities accept Commerce students with Maths for BCA. Always check the specific university's eligibility. 
Is Humanities a good choice? 
Yes. Humanities leads to law, psychology, journalism, design, economics, public policy and civil services, among others. It is a strong choice for students who enjoy reading, writing, debate and understanding society. 
Should I take PCMB? 
Only if you enjoy both Maths and Biology and can handle a heavier workload. PCMB keeps engineering and medicine open, but most students do better choosing the one they are more drawn to.

## CUET UG: what Class 12 students should know 

The Common University Entrance Test (CUET UG) is now the main entry route into central universities and many state and private universities across India. If you are in Class 12 and plan to study in India, there is a good chance you will need it. 

By Om Garg , Founder, MyUniMentor · Updated 20 Nov 2026 · 8 min read 

## What is CUET UG? 

CUET UG is a national entrance test conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) for undergraduate admissions. Central universities such as Delhi University, BHU, JNU and Jamia admit students through it, and a large number of state, deemed and private universities also accept CUET scores. 

It is a computer-based test with multiple-choice questions. You choose which subjects to appear in, based on the course and universities you are targeting. 

## How the exam is structured 

The test has three kinds of papers. You don't take all of them. You pick the ones your chosen courses ask for, up to five subjects in total. 

Section What it tests 

Languages Reading comprehension, vocabulary and grammar in English, Hindi or another listed language 

Domain subjects Subjects like Accountancy, Physics, History or Economics, based on the Class 12 NCERT syllabus 

General Test General knowledge, current affairs, reasoning and basic maths (up to Class 8 level) 

In the 2026 cycle, each paper had 50 questions to be answered in 60 minutes. Each correct answer earned 5 marks and each wrong answer cost 1 mark, so guessing has a price. NTA can change the pattern, so always check the official information bulletin for your year on cuet.nta.nic.in . 

## How to choose your CUET subjects 

This is where many students make mistakes. Each university sets its own subject requirements for each course. A wrong subject choice can make you ineligible, even with a great score. 

- Shortlist your courses and universities first. For example, B.Com (Hons) at three universities. 

- Read each course's CUET requirement on the university's admission page. Some want a language plus specific domain subjects; some accept the General Test. 

- Pick subjects that cover all your targets. Prefer subjects you studied in Class 12, since domain papers follow that syllabus. 

- Keep one backup combination in mind in case your first-choice course doesn't work out. 

MyUniMentor tip 
Make a simple table: courses in rows, required CUET subjects in columns. If one subject combination ticks every row, that's your choice. If not, you need to prioritise. 

## When does CUET happen? 

Registration usually opens early in the year, and the exam is usually held in May, after Class 12 board exams. Check the latest expected dates on our entrance exam calendar . 

## How to prepare 

- Your NCERT books are the base. Domain papers follow the Class 12 NCERT syllabus, so board preparation and CUET preparation overlap a lot. 

- Practise under time. 50 questions in 60 minutes means speed and accuracy both matter. 

- Avoid blind guesses. With negative marking, skip questions you can't narrow down. 

- Read daily for the General Test. A few minutes of news each day builds the current affairs you need. 

## After the result 

CUET only gives you a score. Admission happens through each university's own process. Delhi University, for example, runs its own online allocation system. Other universities have their own forms, deadlines and merit lists. Missing a university's registration window can cost you a seat even with a strong score, so track every deadline.

## Questions students ask 
Still unsure? Call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070 . 
Is CUET compulsory for all universities? 
No. CUET is required by central universities and accepted by many state, deemed and private universities. Some private universities run their own entrance tests or admit on Class 12 marks. Check each university's admission page. 
How many subjects can I choose in CUET UG? 
In recent cycles, students could choose up to five subjects across languages, domain subjects and the General Test. Check the latest NTA bulletin for your year. 
Is there negative marking in CUET? 
Yes. In the 2026 cycle, a correct answer earned 5 marks and a wrong answer cost 1 mark. Unanswered questions score zero. 
Do I need coaching for CUET? 
Not necessarily. Domain papers follow the NCERT Class 12 syllabus. Many students prepare well with NCERT books, practice papers and timed mock tests.

## BBA vs B.Com: which one fits you? 

BBA and B.Com are two of the most popular courses after Class 12, especially for Commerce students. They sound similar, but they train you for different kinds of work. Here's how to tell which one fits you. 

By Om Garg , Founder, MyUniMentor · Updated 20 Nov 2026 · 6 min read 

## The short answer 

B.Com goes deep into accounting, finance, taxation and commerce. It suits students who like numbers and want careers like Chartered Accountancy or finance. 

BBA is about how organisations are run: management, marketing, people and strategy. It suits students who want to manage teams, start a business, or move into an MBA. 

## Side by side 

BBA B.Com 

Focus Management, marketing, HR, operations, entrepreneurship Accounting, finance, taxation, economics, business law 

Style of learning Case studies, presentations, projects, internships Concepts, numerical problems, theory 

Duration 3 years (4 years with honours at many universities under NEP) 3 years (4 years with honours at many universities under NEP) 

Stream Any stream Commerce is preferred; some universities accept other streams 

Natural next step MBA, or a job in sales, marketing, HR or operations CA, CS, CMA, M.Com, MBA (Finance), or finance and accounts roles 

## Choose BBA if you… 

- Enjoy leading groups, presenting and convincing people 

- Want to run your own business or a family business one day 

- Are planning an MBA and want a management foundation 

- Prefer practical, project-based learning over heavy theory 

## Choose B.Com if you… 

- Enjoy Accountancy and are comfortable with numbers 

- Are planning CA, CS or CMA alongside or after your degree 

- Want a career in banking, taxation, audit or financial analysis 

- Like understanding exactly how money moves through a business 

MyUniMentor tip 
Don't choose on the name of the degree alone. Look at the specialisations a university offers, such as BBA in Business Analytics or B.Com in FinTech. The specialisation often matters more than the degree title. 

## Admissions and entrance exams 

Many universities admit BBA and B.Com students through CUET UG . Some run their own tests or admit on Class 12 marks. If you are aiming for a five-year Integrated Programme in Management (IPM) at an IIM, you'll need IPMAT or JIPMAT. See our exam calendar for dates. 

## Does one pay more than the other? 

Starting roles depend far more on your college, internships, skills and specialisation than on the degree name. A B.Com graduate who clears CA, and a BBA graduate who goes on to a strong MBA, can both build excellent careers. Choose the path you'll enjoy working hard at. 

Want a detailed look? Read our course guides on BBA after 12th and B.Com (Hons) after 12th .

## Questions students ask 
Still unsure? Call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070 . 
Can a Science student do BBA or B.Com? 
Yes. BBA is open to all streams at most universities. Many universities also accept Science students for B.Com, though some prefer Commerce. Check each university's eligibility. 
Is Maths required for BBA? 
Most universities do not require Maths for BBA. Some business analytics or finance specialisations and the IPMAT for IIM programmes expect Maths. Check the course you're targeting. 
Which is better for CA, BBA or B.Com? 
B.Com overlaps much more with the CA syllabus, which makes it the more common choice for CA aspirants. 
Is BBA good for an MBA? 
Yes. BBA gives a strong management foundation for an MBA, but MBA admissions are open to graduates of any discipline.

## 12 questions to ask a university before you apply 

Every university brochure looks impressive. The real difference shows up when you ask the right questions. Use this list at university stalls, on campus visits and on admission calls before you pay anything. 

By Om Garg , Founder, MyUniMentor · Updated 20 Nov 2026 · 7 min read 

## Recognition and quality 

- Is the university recognised by the UGC? You can check the official list on the UGC website. For engineering and management, also ask whether the programme is approved by AICTE where it applies. 

- What is its NAAC grade, and is it current? NAAC accreditation is valid for a fixed period. Ask for the grade and the year it was awarded. 

- Does it appear in the NIRF rankings? NIRF is the Government of India's ranking framework. Check the category relevant to your course. 

## Placements and outcomes 

- What percentage of students in my course were placed last year? Ask for your specific programme, not the whole university. 

- What was the median package, not just the highest? The highest package is one student. The median tells you what a typical student gets. 

- Which companies hired from my course, and for which roles? Ask for a list from the last two years. 

- Are internships part of the programme? Ask how the university helps students find them. 

MyUniMentor tip 
Ask to speak to a current student or a recent graduate from your course. Ten minutes with them will tell you more than any brochure. 

## Teaching and campus 

- Who teaches the core subjects? Ask about faculty qualifications and industry experience in your department. 

- What is the hostel like, and is it guaranteed? Ask about rooms, food, safety, curfew rules and whether first-year students get a hostel seat. 

## Money 

- What is the total cost for the full course? Ask for tuition plus hostel, mess, exam fees, uniforms, laptops and any one-time charges, for every year. 

- What scholarships are available, and what do I need to keep them? Many scholarships need a minimum score every semester. Get the conditions in writing. 

- What is the refund policy if I withdraw? The UGC has issued guidelines on fee refunds. Ask how the university applies them before you pay. 

## How to use this list 

Take the same questions to every university on your shortlist and write the answers side by side. The best choice is usually clear once you compare honestly. A MyUniMentor counsellor can help you build and compare your shortlist. 

Met a university at our School Career Guidance Summit ? These are the questions to ask at their stall.

## Questions students ask 
Still unsure? Call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070 . 
How do I check if a university is recognised? 
The University Grants Commission (UGC) publishes the list of recognised universities on its official website. Check that the university appears there before applying. 
Is the highest placement package a good measure? 
Not on its own. The highest package is usually one student. Ask for the median package and the percentage of students placed in your specific course. 
What costs should I ask about besides tuition? 
Hostel, mess, exam fees, registration, uniforms, laptops, transport and any one-time charges. Ask for the total cost for the full course, year by year. 
Can I get my fees back if I change my mind? 
The UGC has issued guidelines on fee refunds when students withdraw. Ask the university how it applies them and get the refund policy in writing before paying.

## Engineering branches explained for Class 12 students 

Most students choose an engineering branch based on what's popular this year. But four years is a long time to study something you don't enjoy. Here is what each major branch actually involves, so you can choose for yourself. 

By Om Garg , Founder, MyUniMentor · Updated 20 Nov 2026 · 8 min read 

## Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) 

Programming, data structures, algorithms, databases, operating systems, networks and software development. CSE suits students who enjoy logical problem-solving and can spend long hours building and debugging code. It leads to software development, product engineering and many other tech roles. See our B.Tech CSE course guide . 

## CSE specialisations: AI, Data Science, Cyber Security 

Many universities now offer CSE with a specialisation, or separate branches like Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, or Data Science. The core is still computer science, with extra courses in the specialisation. These suit students who are very sure of their interest. If you are unsure, core CSE keeps more options open. 

## Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE) 

Circuits, semiconductors, signal processing, communication systems and embedded systems. ECE suits students who like Physics and want to understand how devices work, from phones to chips. Graduates work in electronics, telecom, chip design and also in software. 

## Electrical Engineering (EE) 

Power systems, machines, control systems and power electronics. EE suits students interested in energy, electric vehicles and renewable power. It is also a common route into public sector jobs. 

## Mechanical Engineering 

Mechanics, thermodynamics, manufacturing, machine design and robotics. Mechanical suits students who like seeing how physical things move and work. It leads to manufacturing, automobiles, aerospace and design roles. 

## Civil Engineering 

Structures, construction, transport, water resources and environmental engineering. Civil suits students who want to build infrastructure such as bridges, roads and buildings. Many graduates work in construction, consulting and government departments. 

## Other branches worth knowing 

- Chemical Engineering: processes in industries like pharmaceuticals, energy and materials 

- Biotechnology: biology combined with engineering, open to PCM students at many universities 

- Aerospace and Automobile Engineering: specialised branches for aircraft and vehicles 

MyUniMentor tip 
Look up the actual subjects in each branch's syllabus on the university website. If the subject names excite you, that's a good sign. If they bore you on paper, they'll bore you in class. 

## Branch or college: which matters more? 

There's no single answer. If you're sure about a branch, choose the best college that offers it. If you are unsure, a stronger college with a broader branch can give you more options later, through electives and minors. What matters is that you'll be motivated for four years. 

## How admissions work 

IITs admit through JEE Advanced. NITs, IIITs and many other institutes admit through JEE Main. Many private universities accept JEE Main scores, run their own entrance tests, or consider Class 12 marks. See our 2027 exam calendar for dates, and remember: B.Tech requires Physics, Chemistry and Maths in Class 12.

## Questions students ask 
Still unsure? Call or WhatsApp +91 74175 57070 . 
Which engineering branch is best? 
No branch is best for everyone. CSE is the most in-demand, but ECE, Electrical, Mechanical and Civil all lead to strong careers. Choose the branch whose subjects genuinely interest you. 
Is CSE with AI better than core CSE? 
Not necessarily. AI and Data Science specialisations add focused courses, but core CSE covers the same foundations and keeps more options open. Choose a specialisation only if you are sure of your interest. 
Can I get into software jobs from ECE or EE? 
Yes. Many ECE and Electrical graduates move into software roles, especially if they build programming skills during college. 
Do I need JEE Main for private universities? 
Not always. Many private universities accept JEE Main scores, but many also run their own entrance tests or admit on Class 12 marks. Check each university.

## Careers after PCB beyond MBBS 

For many PCB students, MBBS feels like the only option. It isn't. Biology opens doors to dozens of healthcare, science and research careers, many of them in high demand. Here are twelve worth knowing. 

By Om Garg , Founder, MyUniMentor · Updated 20 Nov 2026 · 7 min read 

## Through NEET UG 

These courses usually admit students through NEET UG, the same exam used for MBBS. 

- BDS (Dentistry): five years including internship. Graduates practise as dentists or specialise further. 

- BAMS, BHMS, BUMS (AYUSH): degrees in Ayurveda, Homoeopathy and Unani medicine, with clinical practice and hospital roles. 

- BVSc and AH (Veterinary Science): treat animals, work in livestock, wildlife or public health. Many veterinary seats are filled through NEET. 

- B.Sc Nursing: many institutes use NEET or their own entrance test. Nurses are in demand in India and abroad. 

## Healthcare without NEET at many universities 

- Physiotherapy (BPT): help patients recover movement after injury or surgery. Strong demand in hospitals, sports and clinics. 

- Pharmacy (B.Pharm): medicines, drug development and the pharma industry. Open to PCB and PCM students. 

- Allied Health Sciences: Medical Lab Technology, Radiology and Imaging, Optometry, Operation Theatre Technology and more. These are essential hospital roles. 

- Nutrition and Dietetics: work in hospitals, sports, wellness and food industries. 

MyUniMentor tip 
Admission rules vary by university and state. Some allied health courses accept Class 12 marks; others use NEET or their own test. Always check eligibility on the university's admission page. 

## Science and research 

- Biotechnology and Microbiology: labs, research, pharma and agriculture. A good fit for students who enjoy experiments. 

- BS-MS at IISERs: research-focused programmes in the sciences. Admission is through the IISER Aptitude Test. 

- Forensic Science: scientific analysis for investigations, in labs and government agencies. 

## Mind and society 

- Psychology: understanding behaviour and mental health. A path to counselling and clinical psychology with further study. 

## How to choose 

Think about what drew you to Biology. If it was helping people, look at physiotherapy, nursing, allied health or psychology. If it was curiosity about how life works, look at biotechnology or research. If you want to treat patients as a doctor, BDS and AYUSH are strong paths through NEET. 

Talk to a counsellor to map your options with your NEET score and budget.

What can I do after PCB if I don't get MBBS? 
BDS, AYUSH courses, veterinary science, nursing, physiotherapy, pharmacy, allied health sciences, biotechnology, nutrition, forensic science, psychology and research programmes are all strong options. 
Which PCB courses don't need NEET? 
Many universities admit students to physiotherapy, pharmacy, allied health, biotechnology, psychology and nutrition without NEET. Rules vary by university and state, so check eligibility for each. 
Is BDS a good option? 
Yes, for students who want to practise as clinicians. BDS is a five-year programme including internship, and dentists can practise or specialise further. 
Can PCB students do engineering? 
Most B.Tech programmes require Maths in Class 12. Some universities offer Biotechnology or related programmes to PCB students. Check each university's eligibility.

## JEE Main 2027 Session 1: dates, pattern and a checklist 

Registration for JEE Main 2027 Session 1 closes on 22 November 2026. If you are in Class 12 and plan to study engineering, architecture or planning, here is what the official NTA documents say about the dates, the paper and the application, in one place. 

By Om Garg , Founder, MyUniMentor · Updated 20 Nov 2026 · 6 min read 

## JEE Main 2027 at a glance 

JEE Main is conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) . It is the entrance exam for B.E./B.Tech, B.Arch and B.Planning at NITs, IIITs and many other institutes, and it is also the first step towards JEE Advanced for the IITs. In 2027 it is held in two sessions, January and April. You do not have to take both. If you appear in both, NTA considers the better of your two scores. 

All dates below are from the JEE Main 2027 Information Bulletin and the public notice of 24 October 2026 on jeemain.nta.nic.in . 

## Session 1 dates 

Step Date 

Online application 24 October to 22 November 2026 (up to 11:50 pm) 

Last date for fee payment 22 November 2026 (up to 11:50 pm) 

Application with late fee 23 to 26 November 2026 (up to 11:50 pm) 

Correction window 27 to 29 November 2026 (up to 11:50 pm) 

City of exam announced 30 December 2026 

Admit card 13 January 2027 

Exam dates 20, 21, 22, 23, 24 and 28 January 2027 

The exam runs in two shifts: 9 am to 12 noon and 3 pm to 6 pm. Your shift and date are given on your admit card. 

For Session 2, the bulletin gives a tentative application window of 5 January to 3 February 2027 and exam dates of 2 to 7 April 2027. NTA will publish a separate notice for Session 2, and you can apply with the same application number. 

## What the paper looks like 

JEE Main has separate papers for each course. Most students take Paper 1. 

Paper For What it has 

Paper 1 B.E./B.Tech Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry. Each subject has 20 multiple-choice questions (Section A) and 5 numerical questions (Section B). 75 questions, 300 marks, 3 hours, computer-based. 

Paper 2A B.Arch Mathematics, Aptitude Test and a Drawing Test. Maths and Aptitude are computer-based; Drawing is on paper, on an A4 drawing sheet. 400 marks. 

Paper 2B B.Planning Mathematics, Aptitude Test and planning-based questions, all computer-based. 100 questions, 400 marks. 

Marking: a correct answer gets +4 and a wrong answer gets –1, in both the multiple-choice and the numerical sections. Unanswered questions get 0. Numerical answers are rounded off to the nearest integer. So a careless guess in the numerical section costs you a mark too. 

In Paper 1, if two students have the same total score, NTA breaks the tie using the Mathematics score first, then Physics, then Chemistry. 

The paper is available in 13 languages: English, Hindi, Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu and Urdu. 

## Before you apply: a checklist 

- Sign in through MeriPehchaan. Registration uses the MeriPehchaan single sign-on, which works with DigiLocker, JanParichay and e-Pramaan. Identity is checked by eKYC using Aadhaar, PAN, driving licence or APAAR. 

- Check your details. Make sure your name, date of birth and other details in the form are correct before you submit. Check spellings carefully. 

- Get your photo right. The bulletin asks for a recent colour photo in JPG/JPEG, between 10 kB and 200 kB, with 80% of the face visible (including ears, without a mask) against a white background. A live photo is also taken while filling the form. 

- Scan the rest. Signature in JPG/JPEG between 10 kB and 100 kB. Class 10 certificate and, if applicable, disability certificate as PDF between 50 kB and 300 kB. 

- Choose four cities with care. You can pick up to four exam cities from the list in the bulletin. Pick places you can reach easily early on exam day. 

- Submit only one form. NTA warns that multiple forms can lead to strict action. If you need to start again, NTA allows a fresh form for Session 1 before the deadline, but only the last form with a successful fee payment counts, and the earlier fee is not refunded. 

- Save your confirmation page. You don't need to post any documents to NTA. Keep a printout and a PDF of the confirmation page. 

MyUniMentor tip 
Don't wait for the last evening. Payment gateways and the portal slow down close to a deadline. Finish your form and payment a few days early, then use the correction window (27–29 November) only if you spot a mistake. NTA lists which fields can be corrected when the window opens. 

## How to use the time until January 

- Plan around your boards. Session 1 falls in the middle of your Class 12 board preparation. Keep revising board topics alongside JEE practice; much of the syllabus overlaps. 

- Practise in the real format. Three hours on a computer is different from a paper test. Take timed mock tests and practise the numerical section separately. 

- Watch accuracy. With –1 for every wrong answer, skipping a question you can't narrow down is often the better choice. 

- Treat Session 1 as a real attempt. If it goes well, you have more time for boards. If not, you still have Session 2 in April. 

## Think beyond the exam 

A JEE score is one part of the decision. The branch and the institute matter just as much. Read our guides to engineering branches and B.Tech CSE after 12th , and keep the other dates in view on our entrance exam calendar . If you are unsure which exams and courses fit you, book a free counselling session . 

Dates and rules can change. Always confirm on jeemain.nta.nic.in before you act.

What is the last date to apply for JEE Main 2027 Session 1? 
The last date is 22 November 2026, up to 11:50 pm, including fee payment. Applications with a late fee are accepted from 23 to 26 November 2026. 
When is JEE Main 2027 Session 1?

## Entrance exam deadlines from late November to January 

The next few weeks are the busiest stretch of the admission year. Several applications close, correction windows open and the first entrance exams begin, all while you revise for your boards. Here is every date in one place, taken from the official websites on 23 November 2026. 

By Om Garg , Founder, MyUniMentor · Updated 23 Nov 2026 · 6 min read 

## Why these weeks matter 

Most students miss a deadline not because they forgot the exam, but because they forgot a smaller step: the late-fee window, the correction window or the admit card. Each of these has its own date, and some of them are only a few days long. If you miss a correction window, for example, you may not get another chance to fix a mistake in your form. 

All dates below come from the official websites of each exam. Keep our entrance exam calendar open as well; we check it against the official sites regularly. 

## All the dates in one table 

Date What happens Exam 

Until 24 Nov 2026 Online application (regular) NIFT Entrance Exam 2027 

25 Nov 2026, 5 pm Last date to apply for entrance-test programmes CHRIST University 

23–26 Nov 2026 Application with late fee (up to 11:50 pm) JEE Main 2027 Session 1 

25–29 Nov 2026 Application with late fee NIFT Entrance Exam 2027 

27–29 Nov 2026 Correction window (up to 11:50 pm) JEE Main 2027 Session 1 

30 Nov 2026, 11:59 pm Last date to apply for B.Des NID DAT 2027 

30 Nov–2 Dec 2026 Correction window (no further chance after this) NIFT Entrance Exam 2027 

3 Dec 2026, 11 pm Entrance test admit card CHRIST University 

5 Dec 2026 Online entrance test CHRIST University 

6 Dec 2026, 2–4 pm Exam CLAT 2027 

6 Dec 2026, 5 pm Last date to apply for non-entrance-test programmes CHRIST University 

11–13 Dec 2026 Skill assessment, micro presentation and interview CHRIST University 

21 Dec 2026, 10 pm Final selection list CHRIST University 

30 Dec 2026 Exam city announced JEE Main 2027 Session 1 

10 Jan 2027 Exam (tentative, as per the NTA exam calendar) NIFT Entrance Exam 2027 

13 Jan 2027 Admit card JEE Main 2027 Session 1 

17 Jan 2027, 9 am–12 noon Exam UCEED 2027 

20–24 and 28 Jan 2027 Exam JEE Main 2027 Session 1 

## JEE Main 2027 Session 1 

The regular application closed on 22 November 2026. According to the NTA information bulletin on jeemain.nta.nic.in , you can still apply with a late fee from 23 to 26 November 2026, up to 11:50 pm. The correction window runs from 27 to 29 November 2026. NTA will announce your exam city on 30 December 2026 and release admit cards on 13 January 2027. 

If you miss Session 1, there is still Session 2. The bulletin gives a tentative application window of 5 January to 3 February 2027 and exam dates of 2 to 7 April 2027. Our JEE Main Session 1 guide covers the paper pattern and a form checklist. 

## NIFT Entrance Exam 2027 

NTA extended the NIFT application deadline in a notice dated 14 November 2026. The revised schedule on exams.nta.nic.in/niftee is: online application until 24 November 2026, late fee from 25 to 29 November 2026, and corrections from 30 November to 2 December 2026. The notice says no further correction opportunity will be given after that. The NTA exam calendar lists the exam on 10 January 2027 and marks its dates as tentative. 

## NID DAT 2027 and UCEED 2027 

For B.Des at the National Institute of Design, the last date to submit the online application is 30 November 2026, 11:59 pm, according to admissions.nid.edu . Check the same site for the Prelims date and your admit card after you apply. 

UCEED 2027 registration, including the late-fee window, closed on 10 November 2026. If you registered, the exam is on Sunday, 17 January 2027, from 9 am to 12 noon ( uceed.iitb.ac.in ). Read our B.Des guide to compare design programmes. 

## CHRIST University and CLAT 

CHRIST (Deemed to be University) runs its own selection process for UG 2027. Its official dates page lists 25 November 2026, 5 pm, as the last day to apply for entrance-test programmes. The online test is on 5 December 2026, the admit card comes out on 3 December, and skill assessment, micro presentation and interviews run from 11 to 13 December. The final selection list is published on 21 December 2026. Programmes without an entrance test accept applications until 6 December 2026. 

CLAT 2027 applications closed on 31 October 2026. The exam is on Sunday, 6 December 2026, from 2 pm to 4 pm, according to the Consortium of NLUs . See our law after 12th guide for what comes after CLAT. 
MyUniMentor tip 
Put every date from the table into your phone calendar today, with a reminder two days before. Treat correction windows as real deadlines: open your submitted form, check your name, date of birth, category and exam city, and fix mistakes while you still can. Do this for one exam at a time so nothing gets mixed up. 

## What has not been announced yet 

As of 23 November 2026, NTA has not announced the dates for NEET UG 2027 or CUET UG 2027 on neet.nta.nic.in and cuet.nta.nic.in . JEE Advanced 2027 is scheduled for 23 May 2027 ( jeeadv.ac.in ). We add new dates to the exam calendar as soon as they are official. Our CUET guide explains how the exam works in the meantime. 

## Balancing forms and board preparation 

- Batch the admin. Set aside one evening a week for forms, payments and downloads, and keep the rest of the week for study. 

- Keep one folder. Save every confirmation page, application number and password in one place, on paper and on your phone. 

- Don't apply for everything. Each exam needs preparation time. Pick the exams that match the courses you actually want. 

If you are not sure which of these exams are worth your time, book a free counselling session and a counsellor will build an exam plan with you. Dates can change, so always confirm on the official website before you act.

## Class 12 board exams 2027: date sheets, results and what comes next 

Board exams are only a few months away. Here is what each board has officially published so far, with full subject-wise date sheets, how results come out, what you can do if your marks are lower than expected, and why your board marks still matter for JEE and CUET admissions. Everything here is taken from the official websites on 24 November 2026. 

By Om Garg , Founder, MyUniMentor · Updated 24 Nov 2026 · 7 min read 

## Date sheets: what each board has published 

CBSE Class 12 starts on 16 February 2027 and ISC on 9 February 2027. We have copied every subject from the official date sheets into searchable pages, where you can also add your own papers to your phone calendar: 

- CBSE Class 12 date sheet 2027 : 16 February to 9 April, all 121 subjects 

- ISC Class 12 timetable 2027 : 9 February to 8 April, every paper 

- CBSE Class 10 date sheet 2027 : 16 February to 9 March, all 83 subjects 

- ICSE Class 10 timetable 2027 : 15 February to 31 March, every paper 

Always check your admit card and your board’s own website as well. Copies shared on WhatsApp are often old or edited. 

Board 2027 Class 12 date sheet Where to get it 

CBSE Published on 6 November 2026 as “Date Sheet for Class X and Class XII Board Examinations, 2027” cbse.gov.in, Examination circulars 

CISCE (ISC) Published on 10 November 2026 as “ISC (Class XII) Year 2027 Examination Timetable and Instructions for Candidates” cisce.org, Regulations and Syllabuses ISC 

MyUniMentor tip 
Once you have your date sheet, put every paper into your phone calendar (our date sheet pages do this for you). Then check it against your entrance exam dates on our exam calendar , so you can see the weeks where both overlap and plan around them early. 

## How results come out 

CISCE says the ISC 2027 results will be declared in April or May 2027. CBSE has not announced a result month yet. For reference, CBSE declared its Class 12 results for 2026 on 13 May 2026 , for about 17.69 lakh candidates. Marksheets were made available in students’ DigiLocker accounts straight after the results, at results.digilocker.gov.in . CISCE publishes its results and notices on cisce.org . 

Before results day, set up your DigiLocker account and keep your roll number and admit card handy. That way you can download your marksheet the moment it is out, which matters if a university asks for it during admissions. 

## If your marks are lower than expected 

Every board gives you a way to have your marks checked, and a second chance to improve them. 

- CBSE: after results, CBSE offers verification of issues and re-evaluation. In 2026, the outcomes were released on DigiLocker from 21 June 2026 onwards. CBSE also holds supplementary exams; it declared the Class 12 supplementary results for 2026 on 12 August 2026. 

- CISCE (ISC): results can be rechecked first; the request must reach CISCE online within four days of the results. Applications for re-evaluation must reach CISCE online within three days of the recheck results. CISCE also runs an improvement exam, in which students can take up to three of the subjects they took in the main exam. 

These windows are short. Read your board’s post-result notice on the day results come out, and apply on time. 

## Why your board marks still matter 

Many students think only entrance exams count. Board marks decide whether you are eligible to use your entrance score at all. 

- NITs, IIITs and other central institutes through JEE Main: you need at least 75% in Class 12 (65% for SC and ST candidates), or a place in the top 20 percentile of your board, according to NTA. JoSAA publishes each board’s top 20 percentile cut-off marks every year on josaa.nic.in . 

- Universities through CUET: each university sets its own minimum Class 12 marks for each course, listed on cuet.nta.nic.in . For example, Delhi Technological University asks for at least 50% and a pass in Mathematics for B.A. (Hons) Economics. 

Our guides to JEE Main 2027 and CUET explain how each exam works. If you are unsure which courses fit your marks and interests, try our psychometric test or book a free counselling session . Dates can change, so always confirm on your board’s website before you act.
